description: Ford's exotic flat-plane crank V8 engine, designed specifically for the Shelby GT350. Features a 180-degree crankshaft like a Ferrari or McLaren, allowing it to rev to 8,250 RPM. The most powerful naturally aspirated production V8 Ford has ever produced, delivering 526 HP at 7,500 RPM.

heritage.significance: First American production flat-plane crank V8, highest-revving Ford production engine
innovations: 8,250 RPM redline - highest of any Ford production engine
Plasma transferred wire arc cylinder coating
Unique firing order for flat-plane configuration

racing_heritage.road_racing: Developed specifically for road course performance
racing_heritage.scca: GT350R competes in SCCA and other racing series
racing_heritage.character: Sounds more like a European exotic than American muscle

base_specifications.valvetrain: DOHC, 4 valves per cylinder, roller finger followers

variants.notes: Same engine as GT350, R model has chassis and aero improvements

crankshaft_design.description: Unlike traditional V8 cross-plane cranks (90-degree), the flat-plane crank has throws 180 degrees apart

common_issues.solution: Normal for high-revving engine, check level frequently

common_issues.description: Engine runs hot under sustained track use
common_issues.solution: Upgraded oil cooler, track day maintenance protocol

notes.sound: The flat-plane crank produces a distinctive exhaust note that's often compared to European exotics like Ferrari rather than traditional American V8s.
notes.track_focus: This engine was designed for road course performance. It excels at high-RPM operation and responds to driver inputs like a European sports car.
notes.not_for_boost: Ford specifically designed this as a NA-only engine. The Predator (supercharged) uses a cross-plane crank for boost compatibility.
